historical_claims_to_preserve: May Checkout supports eligible AU/US business locations and AUD/USD prices, payment mode only, setup/subscription excluded, with Stripe choosing relevant methods in dynamic configuration or the merchant manually listing zip. Keep hosted success_url and embedded return_url distinct (old raw lines 12-51 and 53-104).

May Direct API is legacy but still supported according to the dated notice. Merchant server creates the Intent, typically passes only the client secret for client confirmation and redirects the customer to authenticate and choose Zip payment options. Alternate manual redirect operates with server create-and-confirm, requires_action and next_action.redirect_to_url (old raw lines 123-172, 241-301 and 307-367).

May test success and failure transition from requires_action to succeeded or requires_payment_method respectively. After return retrieve Intent status for display, and use payment_intent.succeeded webhook for completion instead of treating a callback as success (old raw lines 292-305 and 363-381).

Keep this narrower stated example alongside separate November overview domestic-only AU/US customer/account, AUD/USD presentment (raw/stripe-payments-zip-2026-11-07.md lines 112-149); do not transfer the overview's general market labels into legacy request support.

answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/zip/accept-a-payment identifies Zip as a buy now, pay later method in Australia and the US and indexes Checkout and Direct API (new raw lines 5-14). It supplies no payment steps, prerequisites or state transitions. In the May 6 guide, the merchant can configure an eligible Checkout Session in payment mode with AUD or USD line items and dynamic or manually listed methods. The customer authenticates at Zip and the merchant receives an immediate stated success or failure outcome (old raw lines 12-51). May Direct API starts with a merchant-server PaymentIntent and client secret, then Stripe.js confirmZipPayment with return_url or optional server confirmation and next_action.redirect_to_url after requires_action. The client can retrieve status on return, and the guide recommends webhooks for completion. Test outcomes move to succeeded or requires_payment_method (old raw lines 123-172 and 241-373). source-stripe-zip-accept-payment.md reflects both routes but mislabels May legacy support as deprecated and applies return_url to hosted Checkout, whose example actually uses success_url (old raw lines 53-104).
answers.Q2: The change at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/zip/accept-a-payment is navigation/presentation only (new raw lines 9-14). Neither variant body was captured, so the index cannot establish deprecation or any change in prerequisites. Preserve May 6, 2026 Direct API Legacy, currently supported at that date and no longer recommended, with support potentially ending if later deprecated (old raw lines 123-133). A separate November Stripe.js reference still documents confirmZipPayment, but does not demonstrate tested support or the linked body. Correct source-stripe-zip-accept-payment.md to differentiate hosted success_url, embedded Session return_url, and Direct Intent return_url (old raw lines 53-104, 264-301 and 307-329). Keep May Checkout AU/US payment-only eligibility versus the legacy Intent’s stated AUD recipe and avoid reading the generic Invoice footnote as recurring support (old raw lines 22-38, 133-168 and 292-301). Separately, the November method overview and BNPL API matrix mark manual capture unsupported. Preserve root index line 7, Stripe index lines 350-351 and 747, and the BNPL concept route at lines 272-273, with a reciprocal source route and a separate navigation reference.
